newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean overseas bond issue applications fall.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean overseas bond issue applications fall.

text.p: Applications to issue overseas equity-linked-securities from South Korean companies fell 35 percent year-on-year to $354.5 million in the second quarter of 1997, the Korea Securities Dealers' Association said on Tuesday.
This compared with $541.3 million worth of applications a year earlier.

An association statement said sluggish investment in line with a depressed local economy was the major reason behind the sharp fall. It also attributed the decline to slowing demand for Korean bonds due to a slump in the Seoul bourse.
The statement said nine companies planned to issue $284.5 milion worth of convertible bonds and one applied to issue $70 million in depositary receipts.

Dong Ah Construction plans to issue the largest amount, $100 million in convertible bonds to help finance overseas investment. It was followed by Kwangju Bank, which planned to issue $70 million in depositary receipts.
The association said it will issue approvals next week.
